cīna.p: [Ci+na] (pu) CL=10 Ci-caye dīghattaṃ, cayanti ettha ratanānīti cīno, janapado. Ṇvādi. 107.] (1) The place where the jewels gather; Cina-Country; China. (2) Mung bean; Green bean. (3) Lentils; Split pea. See-Cīnaka. Cīna(ti) [cīna+ṇa] (1) Made in Cina Country (China). (2) Made of cloth and garment in Cina-country. (3) People from Cina-country. See-Sakayavanacīnavilāta.
pn:
Cīna. The Pāli name of China. It is several times mentioned in the Milindapañha (121, 327), once as a place where ships congregate (359). Nāgasena speaks (121) of a contemporary Cīnarājā who could charm the ocean by an Act of Truth and could enter the ocean to a distance of one league in his chariot drawn by lions, the waves rolling back at his approach.

The Apadāna (ii.359) speaks of the Cīnaraṭṭha in a list of countries and tribes.

The Commentaries (e.g., Vibh-a.159) speak of the softness of Chinese silk (Cīnapaṭa).
